title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to Automated Lane Keeping Systems (ALKS)
scope_summary: Approves vehicle types with regard to their Automated Lane Keeping System. The ALKS is a driver-activated automated driving system that controls lateral and longitudinal movement for extended periods up to 130 km/h. It applies to vehicles of categories M and N1.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to the type approval of vehicles of Category M and N1 with regards to their Automated Lane Keeping System.
applies_to_components: Automated Lane Keeping System (ALKS) as a whole
ALKS electronic control system (sensors, electronic control units, actuators, transmission links, mechanical/electro-pneumatic/electro-hydraulic elements)
Sensing system and its detection range / self-check
Lateral and longitudinal control (steering and braking/acceleration actuation) performing the Dynamic Driving Task
Lane Change Procedure function including system-controlled direction indicator lamps
Emergency Manoeuvre and Evasive Lane Crossing function
Activation/deactivation controls and driver input / system override
Human Machine Interface and information to the driver, including on-board displays used for non-driving activities
Object and Event Detection and Response (OEDR)
Data Storage System for Automated Driving (DSSAD)
Cyber security and software update provisions for the ALKS
relation_to_other_regulations: Described as the first regulatory step for an automated driving system as defined in ECE/TRANS/WP.29/1140.
Vehicle categories are as defined in the Consolidated Resolution R.E.3 (ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.6).

Paragraph 9 (Cyber Security and Software-Updates) relates to cyber security and software update requirements; the information document allows a cross-reference to the cyber regulation (UN R155), and software updates are linked to UN R156 provisions.
Annex 4 sets special requirements for the safety aspects of electronic control systems, a complex-electronic-systems audit similar to those used in other UN Regulations, e.g. UN R79 and UN R13-H.
The Lane Change Procedure uses direction indicator lamps, whose installation is governed by UN R48.
Approval numbers currently correspond to the 01 series of amendments.
Paragraph 4.5 allows combined approval marks with other UN Regulations.

defined_terms.label: Automated Lane Keeping System
defined_terms.definition: A driver-activated system that keeps the vehicle within its lane at travelling speeds of 130 km/h or less by controlling lateral and longitudinal movements for extended periods without further driver input.

defined_terms.term: Vehicle Type with regard to ALKS
defined_terms.label: Vehicle type
defined_terms.definition: Vehicles not differing in vehicle features significantly influencing ALKS performance or in ALKS system characteristics and design.

defined_terms.label: Transition demand
defined_terms.definition: A logical and intuitive procedure by which the system requests transfer of the Dynamic Driving Task from automated control to the human driver.

defined_terms.label: Transition phase
defined_terms.definition: The duration of the transition demand.

defined_terms.label: Planned event
defined_terms.definition: A situation known in advance, such as a highway exit, that requires a transition demand.

defined_terms.label: Unplanned event
defined_terms.definition: A situation unknown in advance but very likely to happen that requires a transition demand, such as road construction, bad weather or missing lane markings.

defined_terms.label: Imminent collision risk
defined_terms.definition: A situation leading to a collision that cannot be avoided by a braking demand lower than 5 m/s2.

defined_terms.label: Minimum Risk Manoeuvre
defined_terms.definition: A risk-minimising procedure performed automatically by the system after an unanswered transition demand or a severe ALKS or vehicle failure.

defined_terms.label: Emergency Manoeuvre
defined_terms.definition: A manoeuvre performed by the system at imminent collision risk to avoid or mitigate a collision.

defined_terms.label: Specified maximum speed
defined_terms.definition: The manufacturer-declared speed up to which the system operates under optimum conditions.

defined_terms.label: Maximum operational speed
defined_terms.definition: The speed selected by the system, based on sensing capability and environmental conditions, up to which the system may be active.

defined_terms.label: Present speed
defined_terms.definition: The current speed selected by the system due to traffic.

defined_terms.label: Detection range
defined_terms.definition: The distance at which the sensing system can reliably recognise a target and generate a control signal, accounting for lifetime deterioration.

defined_terms.label: ALKS failure
defined_terms.definition: Any single failure specific to ALKS operation, such as a single sensor failure or loss of necessary calculation data.

defined_terms.label: Failure mode
defined_terms.definition: The operation status in which the system operates with an ALKS failure.

defined_terms.label: Severe ALKS failure
defined_terms.definition: A very-low-probability ALKS-specific failure that affects safe operation in failure mode, for example of an electronic control unit.

defined_terms.label: Severe vehicle failure
defined_terms.definition: A vehicle failure, such as loss of power supply, braking failure or sudden tyre pressure loss, that affects both ALKS DDT performance and manual operation.

defined_terms.label: Self-check
defined_terms.definition: An integrated function that continuously checks for system failures and for the sensing system's detection range.

defined_terms.label: System override
defined_terms.definition: A driver input to a control that has priority over the system's longitudinal or lateral control while the system is active.

defined_terms.label: Dynamic Driving Task
defined_terms.definition: The control and execution of all longitudinal and lateral movements of the vehicle.

defined_terms.label: Data Storage System for Automated Driving
defined_terms.definition: A system that enables determination of interactions between the ALKS and the human driver.

defined_terms.label: Lifetime of the system
defined_terms.definition: The period during which the ALKS is available as a function on the vehicle.

defined_terms.label: Occurrences
defined_terms.definition: Events or incidents that require storage within the DSSAD.

defined_terms.label: R157 Software Identification Number
defined_terms.definition: A manufacturer-defined identifier representing the type-approval-relevant software of the ALKS electronic control system.

defined_terms.label: Electronic control system
defined_terms.definition: A combination of units, such as sensors, ECUs, actuators and transmission links, co-operating by electronic data processing to produce the automated lane keeping function.

defined_terms.label: Software
defined_terms.definition: The part of an electronic control system consisting of digital data and instructions.

defined_terms.label: String instability
defined_terms.definition: Amplification by the following vehicle of a disturbance in the speed profile of the vehicle in front.

defined_terms.label: Starting lane
defined_terms.definition: The lane out of which the ALKS vehicle intends to manoeuvre.

defined_terms.label: Target lane
defined_terms.definition: The lane, hard shoulder, refuge area or area beside the road into which the ALKS vehicle intends to manoeuvre.

defined_terms.label: Evading lane
defined_terms.definition: The lane into which the ALKS vehicle crosses during an evasive lane crossing.

defined_terms.label: Lane Change Procedure
defined_terms.definition: A sequence of operations from system activation to system deactivation of the direction indicator lamps, including suspension of lane keeping, lateral movement and the lane change manoeuvre.

defined_terms.label: Lane Change Manoeuvre
defined_terms.definition: The part of the LCP from the front wheel tyre edge crossing the lane marking until the rear wheels have fully crossed it.

defined_terms.label: Aborted lane change manoeuvre
defined_terms.definition: An LCM that is not completed and returns the vehicle to its original lane.

defined_terms.label: Target stop area
defined_terms.definition: A potential stopping area, such as an emergency lane, hard shoulder, area beside the road, slowest lane or own lane.

defined_terms.label: Beside the road
defined_terms.definition: Road surface beyond the carriageway boundaries that is not a hard shoulder or refuge area.

defined_terms.label: MRM lane change
defined_terms.definition: A lane change procedure performed by the ALKS during a minimum risk manoeuvre.

defined_terms.label: Regular lane change
defined_terms.definition: Any ALKS lane change procedure that is not an MRM lane change.

defined_terms.label: Evasive Lane Crossing
defined_terms.definition: An emergency manoeuvre resulting in the ALKS vehicle crossing a lane marking.

defined_terms.label: Potential Vehicle Presence Area
defined_terms.definition: The speed-dependent area around the vehicle and target lane in which another vehicle could be relevant to an ALKS lane change.

classes_and_variants.name: ALKS capable of an LCP (approval mark symbol "LC")
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: The system is able to perform a Lane Change Procedure (para 4.4.3.1).

classes_and_variants.name: ALKS without lane change capability
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: Lane keeping only; no additional symbol in the approval mark.

classes_and_variants.name: Regular lane change vs MRM lane change
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: Whether the lane change is performed during a minimum risk manoeuvre.

classes_and_variants.name: Performance model 1 / Performance model 2 (Annex 3)
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: The alternative models used to derive the conditions under which collisions are deemed avoidable in traffic-critical scenarios.

classes_and_variants.name: ALKS failure vs severe ALKS failure vs severe vehicle failure
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: Severity of the failure and whether manual operation is also affected; this determines the response (failure mode, transition demand or MRM).

applicability_hints: Any sensor (camera, radar, lidar, ultrasonic), ECU, actuator or transmission link that contributes to the automated lane keeping function is part of the ALKS 'electronic control system' and falls under paras 5, 7, 9 and Annex 4.
Steering, braking and powertrain actuators commanded by the ALKS are in scope through the DDT, EM and MRM requirements.
Direction indicator lamps controlled by the system are relevant when the ALKS performs a Lane Change Procedure (LC variant).
Driver monitoring cameras and sensors, such as eye or head tracking and hands-on detection, fall under the Driver Availability Recognition System (6.1).
Infotainment and on-board displays used for non-driving activities are affected, because they must be automatically suspended when a transition demand is issued (para 6.4 / introduction).
HMI elements such as telltales, displays, acoustic or haptic warning devices and ALKS activation/deactivation switches fall under para 6.
Event or data recorders storing ALKS–driver interaction data fall under the DSSAD requirements (para 8).
ALKS software and its update mechanism, including OTA, are covered by para 9 and the R157SWIN.
Only vehicle categories M and N1 are in scope in this version; N2/N3 are not covered by this text's scope.
Power supply, braking and tyre pressure systems can be relevant indirectly, because their failures count as 'severe vehicle failures' to which the ALKS must respond.
